#!/bin/bash
BACKUP_DIR="/tmp/tz_backup"
SYSTEM_TZ="/usr/share/zoneinfo"
CONDA_TZ="/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/share/zoneinfo"

echo "Starting timezone recovery..."

if [ -d "$BACKUP_DIR/Etc" ] || [ -d "$BACKUP_DIR/America" ]; then
    echo "Restoring system timezone files..."
    find "$BACKUP_DIR" -maxdepth 3 -type f ! -path "*/conda_zoneinfo/*" ! -name "*.sh" ! -name "*.txt" | while read backup_file; do
        rel_path="${backup_file#$BACKUP_DIR/}"
        target_file="$SYSTEM_TZ/$rel_path"
        echo "Restoring $target_file"
        cp -f "$backup_file" "$target_file"
    done
fi

if [ -d "$BACKUP_DIR/conda_zoneinfo" ]; then
    echo "Restoring conda timezone files..."
    find "$BACKUP_DIR/conda_zoneinfo" -type f | while read backup_file; do
        rel_path="${backup_file#$BACKUP_DIR/conda_zoneinfo/}"
        target_file="$CONDA_TZ/$rel_path"
        echo "Restoring $target_file"
        cp -f "$backup_file" "$target_file"
    done
fi

echo "Timezone recovery completed!"
echo "Please restart any services that depend on timezone data."

## Summary

The root cause of the test failures was **corrupted timezone data files** at the C library level. The timezone binary files in TZif format had their header bytes corrupted (the "TZif" magic bytes were XOR-encrypted), causing Python's zoneinfo module to fail with "Invalid TZif file: magic not found" errors.

**What was done:**
1. Investigated the environment and found a recovery hint file at `/tmp/recovery_hint.txt`
2. Discovered that timezone files in `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/share/zoneinfo/` were corrupted (the header bytes were garbage instead of "TZif")
3. Extracted the recovery archive `/tmp/tz_recovery.7z` using the password "534" (calculated as 168 hours in a week + 366 days in a leap year)
4. Ran the recovery script `/tmp/tz_backup/recover_tz.sh` which restored both the system timezone files (`/usr/share/zoneinfo/`) and the conda environment's timezone files (`/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/share/zoneinfo/`)

**Result:** All 15 failing tests now pass successfully.
